question: What is the difference between justification and sanctification?
answer: Justification is what God did for us once for all when we trusted Christ: He declared us righteous, counting the righteousness of His Son as ours. Sanctification is what God is doing in us day by day for the rest of our lives, making us actually holy. As J. C. Ryle wrote in Holiness, justification is the act of God about us, while sanctification is the work of God within us. Confusing the two leads either to fear or to carelessness.

question: What does it mean to be dead to sin and alive to God?
answer: When we were joined to Christ by faith, we were joined to His death and resurrection: "Our old self was nailed to the cross with Him, so that the body of sin would be stripped of its power and we would no longer serve sin as slaves" (Romans 6:6). So Paul tells us to "count yourselves as dead to sin, and as living for God in Christ Jesus" (Romans 6:11). Watchman Nee learned that we count it because it is already true, not to make it true. We fight sin from Christ's victory, not for it.

question: How can a Christian overcome sin in practice?
answer: God has given confession, repentance, accountability and walking in the Spirit. "If we confess our sins, He is faithful and righteous: He will forgive our sins and cleanse us from every kind of wrongdoing" (1 John 1:9), and James urges believers to confess their sins to each other and pray for each other. Above all, "walk by the Spirit, and you will never carry out what the flesh desires" (Galatians 5:16). When we fall, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ, so we get up, confess and go on.
